prompts: I'm inside a nested Python helper called by my instrumented agent. I saw weave.get_current_conversation() in a reference and want to use it instead of passing the conversation object through every function. Is it a real documented API, what does it return, and what happens when no conversation is active? Show a small usage example.

output.answer:
Yes, `weave.get_current_conversation()` is a documented Python API.

**What it returns:** The reference gives the signature `get_current_conversation() → Conversation | None`. It returns the active conversation from a contextvar, or `None` [S1]. The guide says the active conversation is stored in context (a Python `ContextVar`), so code in the same async context can retrieve it without having the object passed in [S2].

**When no conversation is active:** The reference says it returns `None` [S1]. The docs I read don't describe any other outcome, such as an exception. Still, write your helper to handle `None` explicitly. The snapshot also doesn't say what happens when you call it from a different thread or a separately created async context. The guide only promises the "same async context" case [S2][S3].

**Where it applies to your helper:** The guide says the active conversation, turn and LLM call are held in context. You can retrieve them from anywhere in the call stack with `weave.get_current_conversation()`, `weave.get_current_turn()` and `weave.get_current_llm()` [S3]. That includes nested helpers, as long as they run inside the active conversation block.

**Example (adapted from the documented patterns, not run):**

```python
import weave

def helper():
    conversation = weave.get_current_conversation()
    if conversation is None:
        # No active conversation: skip tracing, or handle as you prefer.
        return "no active conversation"

    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="Nested helper turn"):
        return "turn started"

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    helper()      # finds the active conversation
helper()          # outside the block, should hit the None branch
```

I couldn't run this because the Weave SDK isn't available in my offline Python sandbox. It combines `start_conversation`, `conversation.start_turn(user_message=...)` and a `None` check, using the forms shown in the guide [S3][S4]. The `None` return comes from the reference [S1].

**Alternative:** You may not need the conversation object at all. The top-level `weave.start_turn(...)` resolves the active conversation from context and inherits its conversation ID. If no conversation is active, the turn is created without a `conversation_id` and isn't grouped with other turns [S4]. Likewise, `start_llm()` and `start_tool()` can be called without holding a parent reference [S3].

**Next step:** Make sure your helper runs inside the `with weave.start_conversation(...)` block. Then add an explicit `None` check, or call `weave.start_turn(...)` directly.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

### Start a conversation

`start_conversation()` (Python) or `startConversation()` (TypeScript) stamps a `conversation_id` attribute on every child span so that turns are grouped in the Agents tab. If you pass a `conversation_id` / `conversationId`, it must be stable across the lifetime of the conversation. Reuse the same ID to add new turns to an existing conversation. For most agents, use a context manager pattern in Python or a try-finally pattern in TypeScript. The span closes and sends at the end of the block, even if an exception occurs.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]

> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

**What it returns:** The reference gives the signature `get_current_conversation() → Conversation | None`. It returns the active conversation from a contextvar, or `None` [S1]. The guide says the active conversation is stored in context (a Python `ContextVar`), so code in the same async context can retrieve it without having the object passed in [S2].

**When no conversation is active:** The reference says it returns `None` [S1]. The docs I read don't describe any other outcome, such as an exception. Still, write your helper to handle `None` explicitly. The snapshot also doesn't say what happens when you call it from a different thread or a separately created async context. The guide only promises the "same async context" case [S2][S3].

**Where it applies to your helper:** The guide says the active conversation, turn and LLM call are held in context. You can retrieve them from anywhere in the call stack with `weave.get_current_conversation()`, `weave.get_current_turn()` and `weave.get_current_llm()` [S3]. That includes nested helpers, as long as they run inside the active conversation block.

**Example (adapted from the documented patterns, not run):**

```python
import weave

def helper():
    conversation = weave.get_current_conversation()
    if conversation is None:
        # No active conversation: skip tracing, or handle as you prefer.
        return "no active conversation"

    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="Nested helper turn"):
        return "turn started"

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    helper()      # finds the active conversation
helper()          # outside the block, should hit the None branch
```

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

### Context manager or try-finally pattern

For most agents, use a context manager pattern in Python or a try-finally pattern in TypeScript. The span closes and sends at the end of the block, even if an exception occurs.

**What it returns:** The reference gives the signature `get_current_conversation() → Conversation | None`. It returns the active conversation from a contextvar, or `None` [S1]. The guide says the active conversation is stored in context (a Python `ContextVar`), so code in the same async context can retrieve it without having the object passed in [S2].

**When no conversation is active:** The reference says it returns `None` [S1]. It doesn't raise an error, so your helper should check for `None`. The snapshot doesn't say what happens when you call it from a different thread or a separately created async context. The guide only promises the "same async context" case [S2][S3].

**Where it applies to your helper:** The guide says the active conversation, turn and LLM call are held in context. You can retrieve them from anywhere in the call stack with `weave.get_current_conversation()`, `weave.get_current_turn()` and `weave.get_current_llm()` [S3]. That includes nested helpers, as long as they run inside the active conversation block.

**Example (adapted from the documented patterns, not run):**

```python
import weave

def helper():
    conversation = weave.get_current_conversation()
    if conversation is None:
        # No active conversation: skip tracing, or handle as you prefer.
        return "no active conversation"

    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="Nested helper turn") as turn:
        return "turn started"

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    helper()      # finds the active conversation
helper()          # outside the block, should hit the None branch
```
